meetings.headline: Water commissioners approved a pilot-study contract for the Hickory Hills well, a GMC truck bid and a PFAS litigation signing.
meetings.summary: Landowner groups read a letter of conditions on reopening the Hickory Hills well, including lake levels, road damage and discharge, and the exchange turned heated. The board then voted to approve the engineering pilot-study agreement, sign onto PFAS litigation, and award the new truck bid. A Pond View Estates owner asked about water service outside the district, and the board agreed to seek counsel's opinion and to discuss the landowner letter in executive session after January 4th.

meetings.headline: Water district heard a pilot-study plan for the Hickory Hills well; residents pressed on lake levels; cell lease and audit contract moved
meetings.summary: Consultants presented a preliminary scope for a roughly year-long pilot study of iron, manganese and PFAS treatment at the Hickory Hills well, plus lake-level monitoring. Residents of The Woodlands and Hickory Hills raised concerns about truck traffic, trailer placement, discharge location, and whether the pilot would show any lake-level impact. The board also moved to sign a T-Mobile tower lease and the annual audit contract, and the pilot study is to return at the next meeting for final review.

meetings.headline: Water commissioners approved a water rate increase effective January 1, 2023, and OK'd a pilot-study agreement for Hickory Hills well.
meetings.summary: The commissioners discussed and voted a rate increase to cover rising maintenance costs (chemicals, electricity, fuel), with a flyer planned for the January bill. They then moved to have the superintendent sign an engineering agreement with Tighe & Bond for a Hickory Hills well pilot study once counsel approves the legal terms. Other items: PFAS lawsuit, cell tower lease, CDL training idea, and a public comment period that included apologies for a heated prior meeting and a push to post approved minutes online.

budget_items.what_was_said: Rising electricity, chemicals and fuel costs mean projected maintenance expenses will fall short; the rate increase is meant only to cover this, not future increases.
Staff recommended the higher option with a minimum charge and a per-100-cubic-foot tier, to cover the next two quarters' billing.
Examples were given of current versus new bills at different usage levels, with the average user seeing roughly a monthly increase.
The agreement being signed is a baseline for preliminary planning for the pilot study.
A resident asked if the earlier-voted amount depended on a grant; officials said it comes from service connection fees and the aim is to be better positioned for state funding.
Superintendent described charging for records copies per state rules, with a per-page charge noted.
Bid opening set; bidding expected to save money versus buying off the state list.
Outside CDL schools cost several thousand dollars; an in-house trainer program could avoid that.
The district is part of a class action against PFAS manufacturers; settlement shares might follow flow rates.

decisions.decision: Rate increase effective January 1, 2023 (January billing cycle); a flyer explaining it will go with the January bill.
Form a small contact group with one representative each from Hickory Hills, the Woodlands and the Selectmen for the pilot study scope, with documents emailed ahead of meetings.
District will follow state public records rules (950 CMR) as a procedure in the absence of its own policy.
Board will move to post approved minutes on the district website, bringing it up at the next meeting only if there is a reason not to.
Superintendent to speak with the DPW director about a joint CDL training program.
